facts.state_of_play:
At a Senate hearing Wednesday, Fauci invoked the Fifth Amendment 111 times. Republican Sen. Rand Paul led the hearing and said there is a "very real chance" Fauci could be prosecuted. A Senate committee plans a contempt vote next week. Fauci's private notes were also a subject of scrutiny. Legal experts called the Fifth Amendment strategy sound but politically damaging, and the Biden pardon may be tested. Trump said he watched the entire 3-hour-plus hearing.

Todd Blanche has since been sworn in as Attorney General. Hours after his swearing-in, the DOJ Office of Legal Counsel published a memo — signed by AAG T. Elliot Gaiser — arguing that executive privilege can extend to Trump's communications with private advisers, provided those communications are confidential and related to presidential decision-making. The memo would shield those advisers from congressional and legal investigations. The New Republic frames this as Blanche immediately breaking promises made to GOP senators Cornyn and Tillis, who had conditioned their support on written assurances about the Trump-IRS settlement and related matters.

contradictions.text: Ledger held Blanche's nomination was in jeopardy pending promises to Cornyn/Tillis; item asserts Blanche was sworn in and immediately acted contrary to those commitments.

facts.state_of_play: Iran launched ballistic missiles in an attempted surprise attack on US military installations in the Middle East; the US says it thwarted the attack. Trump threatened severe retaliation. A drone struck a US-owned gas storage tanker at Egypt's Damietta port. Oil prices surged 7% above $90/barrel. US oil inventories are at precariously low levels. Internally, Trump is exasperated as top officials cannot agree on an Iran strategy. It has also emerged that during last month's NATO summit in Turkey, the White House carried out an elaborate ruse to protect Trump from a credible Iranian assassination threat: Trump was hidden in an airport catering container and moved to a military jet for a secret flight out of Turkey, while staff and members of the press corps were left aboard Air Force One as unwitting decoys. Trump had publicly told the press he was skipping his newly renovated Qatari-gifted Air Force One to fly the original 'for old time's sake.' Katie Miller, wife of White House deputy chief of staff Stephen Miller, publicly attacked Washington Post reporter Dan Lamothe, who broke the story. The Federal Reserve, chaired by Kevin Warsh, voted 9-3 to hold interest rates steady for the fifth consecutive time, keeping the federal funds rate at 3.5%–3.75%; three members dissented in favor of a quarter-point hike, the first three-dissent vote in a decade. US borrowing costs are at a 19-year high. The Dow closed down over 1,000 points on the news. The hold is seen as a win for Trump, though it contrasts with Warsh's own hawkish rhetoric. F1 is weighing moving its season-closing Middle East races to Europe, with a mid-September decision deadline. Separately, Trump announced a $22.5 billion redesign of Dulles International Airport. In football governance, FIFA President Gianni Infantino has announced a plan to create a new subsidiary to run part of the World Cup and sell a 20% stake to private investors in a venture valued at $20bn, with Joshua Kushner named as the investor; federations have until September 19 to decide. The plan has triggered furious backlash: UEFA has called an emergency meeting of its 55 members for Thursday to coordinate a response, with a European boycott of FIFA tournaments including the Women's World Cup under consideration. During the World Cup, US federal authorities seized 44 drones and $9 million in fake FIFA merchandise in Houston.
